nodes.title: Maitri 2023 Climate Connections Expedition
nodes.reviewDetail: A simulated educator review checked the plain-language reading level, glossary links, Hindi copy and correspondence between narrative claims and graph paths. It is not scientific peer review.
nodes.plainLanguageSummary: A small Indian research team spent the Antarctic summer near Maitri station following a simple question: how do air, ice, lakes and human activity connect? They measured carbon exchange, sea-ice change, weather and traces of microplastics. This demo connects each explanation to the dataset or publication node that supports it.
nodes.hindiSummary: एक भारतीय अनुसंधान दल ने मैत्री स्टेशन के पास अंटार्कटिक ग्रीष्मकाल में यह समझने का प्रयास किया कि हवा, बर्फ, झीलें और मानवीय गतिविधियाँ आपस में कैसे जुड़ी हैं। दल ने कार्बन के आदान-प्रदान, समुद्री बर्फ में बदलाव, मौसम और सूक्ष्म प्लास्टिक के निशानों का अध्ययन किया। यह प्रदर्शन हर सरल व्याख्या को उससे जुड़े डेटासेट या प्रकाशन से जोड़ता है।

myths.claim: Satellite images prove there are hidden pyramids in Antarctica.
myths.rebuttal: Mountain peaks called nunataks can form angular shadows. Shape alone is not evidence of a constructed pyramid; field observations and mapped geology provide the testable explanation.

citation.label: USGS Antarctic geology overview
citation.detail: The institutional landing page resolved; the demo rebuttal is linked to the landform concept node.

myths.claim: Antarctica is surrounded by a secret ice wall.
myths.rebuttal: Antarctica is a mapped continent with ice shelves at parts of its coastline. Satellite observations, navigation and long-running research stations independently document its geography.

citation.label: NASA Earth Observatory Antarctica
citation.detail: The NASA landing page resolved; the claim is traced to the Antarctic geography concept.

myths.claim: One cold day in Antarctica disproves global warming.
myths.rebuttal: Weather describes short-term conditions; climate is a pattern measured over decades. A single local observation cannot establish or overturn a long-term global trend.

citation.label: NASA climate evidence
citation.detail: The NASA evidence page resolved; the distinction is linked to the weather concept and long-term observations.
